steps.detail: Treat the documented silk support as supplied. Flex or unfold on a wet mechanical fixture and compare each path before and after while holding electrical conditions constant.
steps.check: A resistance change is not by itself a measurement of humidity-driven shape or shield performance.

gaps: Silk feedstock and its treatment, in-vivo delivery, catheter procedures and anatomical performance are not modeled. Conventional and compact pad spacing are not interchangeable layouts.

profiles.title: Kirigami-to-helix: flat addresses, deployed compliant geometry
profiles.summary: A patterned spiral trace can deform into a three-dimensional spring. Drawing a helix is not a fabrication flow; the initial planar circuit, temporary carrier and electrical verification remain distinct.

sources.title: Fang et al., kirigami microelectrode arrays (2026)
sources.note: Primary paper identifies a reconfigurable spiral-thread design. The module-level workflow below flags manufacturing details not established in this record.

variants.label: 120-contact small array
variants.description: A reported smaller configuration, not an assumption about the larger fanout.

variants.label: 256-contact array
variants.description: Published higher-count configuration; aggregation across arrays is a separate operation.

variants.label: Parameterized inert spiral coupon
variants.description: Explore turns and clearance while preserving the same endpoints. An assumed metal stack is not attributed to the authors.

steps.title: Freeze planar and deformed geometries
steps.detail: Maintain a distinct planar spiral and a free three-dimensional trace. Define measured versus inferred coordinates wherever the source supplies only drawings.
steps.check: Check that both representations carry the same endpoints and connected components.

steps.title: Require the verified process stack
steps.detail: Metal/dielectric stack, exact masks and release chemistry are not independently reconstructed here. Obtain a documented process before claiming an exact ki-MEA build.
steps.check: Leave missing layers unknown rather than borrowing a stack from another kirigami paper.

steps.title: Make a virtual planar surrogate
steps.detail: For the coupon branch only, use a polymer/metal sandwich with openings and cut gaps as an explanatory comparison. A manufacturing analogue is not evidence of the manuscript's materials.
steps.check: Check fill, trace width, gap and connectivity after pattern transfer in the simplified design.

steps.title: Support, release and deform on an inert fixture
steps.detail: Support free planar members on a removable carrier, then apply a controlled displacement between ends on a phantom fixture. Track strain relative to the selected constitutive model.
steps.check: Compare retained edge continuity before/after deformation. A modeled spring constant is not a measured property of their device.

steps.title: Recheck terminal map and load path
steps.detail: Distinguish an electrical open at a hard anchor from mechanical translation with intact impedance.
steps.check: Report electrical, optical shape and mechanical load independently; no clinical or tissue deployment claim.

gaps: An exact multi-device routing diagram, final implanted positions, material-specific yield and local mechanical calibration are unavailable. Keep the 120/256 references distinct from the teaching coupon.

profiles.title: PMT disk grid and Blackrock pedestal: two research configurations
profiles.summary: Two speech-interface studies identify a custom PMT grid with external Blackrock acquisition. Match the particular grid before inventing a mask, molding process, or connector map.

sources.title: Moses et al., 2021 speech neuroprosthesis
sources.note: Methods and supplementary appendix identify the 128-contact 16 × 8 grid, 4 mm spacing, and connector.

sources.title: Metzger et al., 2023 speech and avatar interface
sources.note: Implanted electrode array section distinguishes 253 disks on a 3 mm pitch, 1 mm exposed and 2 mm overall diameter.

variants.label: 2021: 16 × 8 contacts, 4 mm center pitch
variants.description: 128 total. The implant footprint is not its active center-to-center span.

variants.label: 2023: 253 contacts, 3 mm center pitch
variants.description: 253 disks with separate exposed and overall diameters. No complete rectangular lattice is inferred.

variants.label: Disk-grid teaching coupon
variants.description: A plausible manually assembled surface grid; alloy, jacket and joining details are local assumptions, not PMT factory specifications.

steps.title: Reconstruct only the published contact layout
steps.detail: Store counts, pitch convention and face diameter by study. A non-square count does not license filling or removing nonexistent corners on a guessed rectangular grid.
steps.check: For the 2021 grid, 16 × 8 produces 128. For the 2023 design, keep unknown coordinates unassigned.

steps.title: Receive disk array and pedestal
steps.detail: PMT supplied the electrode grid and Blackrock the separate percutaneous component. Actual molded-layer stack, joint process, die/tooling, alloy lot and production masks are not established by these speech studies.
steps.check: Require the appropriate revision and pinout; a similarly branded grid or pedestal is not a drop-in substitute.

steps.title: Construct an illustrative wired coupon
steps.detail: Seat preformed conductive disks in an insulating carrier fixture, form individual insulated leads, strain-relieve the tail, and leave only the recording faces exposed. This is one possible assembly, not a PMT recipe.
steps.check: Check every disk's exposed face and adjacent insulation separately before joining it to the readout.

steps.title: Verify the cable-to-contact crosswalk
steps.detail: Use an isolated test adapter and one-to-one continuity checks. Preserve left/right orientation and verify the reference and unused pins separately.
steps.check: A swapped disk address must fail even if all channel resistances appear normal.

steps.title: Acquire a known phantom pattern
steps.detail: Apply a known spatial stimulus to an inert fixture; verify raw electrical mapping prior to any feature extraction or decoder. A speech task is not an electrical acceptance test.
steps.check: Open one site and then the whole backend connector; distinguish a localized failure from a total readout loss.

gaps: No as-built manufacturing instructions, vendor wiring diagrams, material certification, implantation procedure or chronic safety inference. Do not borrow dimensions from unrelated PMT products.

profiles.title: INBRAIN graphene interface: nanoporous rGO, not a CLEAR film
profiles.summary: Manchester investigators report a thin flexible interface with twelve 1 mm macrocontacts and 48 separate 25 µm microcontacts made from nanoporous reduced graphene oxide. The grouped microstructures in a macrocontact are not all independent recording channels.

sources.title: Manchester investigators, graphene cortical interface interim abstract (2025)
sources.note: The investigators identify INBRAIN as manufacturer, nanoporous reduced graphene oxide and the macro/micro contact configuration. This is a conference abstract, not a manufacturing traveler.

sources.title: Viana et al., EGNITE nanoporous graphene research microelectrodes (2024)
sources.note: Materials, wafer-scale fabrication and Figure 1: GO filtration/transfer, hydrothermal reduction, PI with Au tracks. An academic comparator, not proof of the production GCI process.

sources.title: Manchester BRC, completed first study (2026)
sources.note: Institutional account establishes that the clinical component was the INBRAIN graphene cortical interface; it does not disclose its factory layout.

variants.label: Clinical investigation GCI, as described
variants.description: 12 macrocontacts plus 48 microcontacts; preserve reported hierarchy. The true factory traveler stays external.

variants.label: EGNITE academic materials comparator
variants.description: Model a related film of reduced graphene oxide on a flexible circuit. Local fixtures map only to modules the evidence actually supports.

variants.label: Replace rGO with transferred planar graphene
variants.description: CLEAR's four CVD graphene transfers and UCSD's doped double layer produce different interface structures; neither is the GCI process.

steps.title: Assign macro and micro recording elements
steps.detail: Distinguish a 1 mm composite macrocontact from a separate 25 µm microcontact. Granularity in a micrograph does not show how every constituent feature is wired.
steps.check: Check the twelve and 48 labels independently; do not multiply the number of macro sites by their sub-features to count acquisition channels.

steps.title: Treat clinical manufacturing as a supplier boundary
steps.detail: Material and some geometric evidence are public; product masks, netlist, deposition sequence, terminations and factory acceptance remain unavailable in these sources.
steps.check: Keep the released product traveler and qualified element-to-acquisition map unclaimed.

steps.title: Fabricate reference polymer wiring
steps.detail: The academic EGNITE architecture places Au routing on PI. Establish the receiver and test metal lines before introducing carbon. This is not a disclosed GCI layer assignment.
steps.check: Check conductor isolation and location of the future carbon-to-metal overlap.

steps.title: Prepare or receive the nanoporous carbon film
steps.detail: The academic paper filters GO flakes to make a transferable film and uses hydrothermal reduction to produce porous conductive material. No qualified GO film line or hydrothermal reactor is established in the register.
steps.check: Inspect witness morphology, thickness and electrical properties; Raman alone cannot prove electrode charge behavior or clinical equivalence.

steps.title: Encapsulate, expose and compare
steps.detail: Follow the academic process class for protected tracks and exposed carbon. On an inert electrolyte fixture, record separate site spectra and trace continuity and compare same-area test contacts.
steps.check: Do not transfer capacity, clinical performance or qualification from the research comparator to the Manchester device.

gaps: Reduced graphene oxide is not synonymous with CVD bilayer graphene or a graphene field-effect transistor. Clinical hardware authenticity and complete manufacturing records are not supplied by the related academic process.

profiles.title: NeuroXess research ECoG: 256-site flex and headstage
profiles.summary: The original Chinese-speech study identifies a 256-contact surface film, flexible printed circuit, processing unit and titanium enclosure. This is not the later fully implanted Triple-F wireless configuration.

sources.title: Real-time decoding of full-spectrum Chinese using brain-computer interface (2025)
sources.note: Materials and Methods and Supplementary Figure S1 identify the 256 contacts, 1.3 mm contact diameter, 3 mm pitch, flex cable, processor and housing.

variants.label: 256-channel study assembly
variants.description: The published architecture; the die process, conductor stack, pin order and bonding chemistry are not recovered.

variants.label: Research flex-grid bench surrogate
variants.description: A deliberately assumed fanout and cable used to test stage interfaces; this is not a NeuroXess commercial process.

variants.label: Copy Triple-F telemetry into this system
variants.description: A separate catalog device and later configuration. Do not borrow its radio, channel count, or full implant enclosure.

steps.title: Capture sensing geometry
steps.detail: Record 256 electrode contacts and distinguish the reported 1.3 mm diameter from the 3 mm center spacing. Reconstruct only published positions; a rectangular raster is not a recovered mask.
steps.check: Validate count and spacing separately from assumed pin order.

steps.title: Represent the device as supplied modules
steps.detail: The paper identifies the array, flexible circuit, processor and titanium enclosure; it does not give a full conductor/dielectric process, chip masks or feedthrough qualification.
steps.check: Demand an as-built bill of materials, layer map and acceptance record before claiming fabrication equivalence.

steps.title: Construct a passive grid stand-in
steps.detail: Pattern an insulated flexible conductor with isolated exposed sites and a separate contact tail. Select and label a representative material stack solely for the stand-in.
steps.check: Reject traces exposed outside their windows and record the assumed layer stack in the fixture data.

steps.title: Interface the cable and test fixture
steps.detail: Use a labeled test adapter to connect known pads to a dummy receiver. The study reports a processing unit; this step does not recreate the actual chip, connector or housing seal.
steps.check: Check mapping and signal path using known inputs before interpreting any feature extraction.

steps.title: Verify acquisition, independently of decoding
steps.detail: Replay a known electrical pattern with raw-channel identifiers; downstream decimation and feature extraction are not wafer manufacturing stages.
steps.check: A working software decoder on injected data cannot establish that the physical array is intact, hermetic or suitable for use.

gaps: The substrate chemistry, detailed array artwork, IC process, wiring pin assignment and seal qualification remain unverified here. No integration with the separate Triple-F configuration is claimed.
